newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Piltel drops 6.06 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Piltel drops 6.06 pct in late trade.

text.p: Cellular phone firm Pilipino Telephone Corp (Piltel) dipped by one peso, or 6.06 percent, to 15.50 pesos in late trade on Wednesday ahead of the expected release of the company's 1996 earnings.

"It's the same old news. People are unconvinced they've sold their cloning problem. Its just plain disenchantment perhaps as the company was expected to grow and post substantial profits," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities Inc.
Piltel's investor relations department said the firm's 1996 results were expected to be released later on Wednesday.
"Maybe its because of their cloning problem and their huge write-off," said Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities.
Piltel said last month it expects its 1996 net income to be "in the vicinity" of 700 million pesos with a provision of 887 million pesos for doubtful accounts.
The cellular phone firm's shares were heavily traded late in the session on Wednesday with 3.98 million shares worth 63.199 million pesos changing hands.
Piltel has been troubled by fradulent calls carried out by organised groups using sophisticated cloning devices.
